terra.problem: The closing maxim about forgetting is generic and preachy.
The text does not say the Israelites stayed where they were.
The text says Othniel prevailed, but does not say he did no bargaining or begging.
The text says Israel cried out, but does not specify that they pleaded.
Saying the land had rest the whole time Othniel was alive extends the forty years of rest to his entire lifetime.
The passage describes what the LORD did, but does not say He spoke a word about it.
The claim that more tribute would not have prompted the king to ask for silence is unsupported.
The explanation invents a general rule that peace talks do not begin with a secret, and assigns a reason for the king's command that the text does not give.
The text does not say nobody was standing guard, and the claim that guards would have asked questions is speculative.
The text does not say there were no marks on the doors.
The text does not say it was a hot day or explicitly give the servants' guess as the reason Ehud gained time.
The servants do not say they think no one is with the king, and the claim that a meeting would have made noise is unsupported.
The text does not say Ehud blew one long sound.
The reference given supports the jawbone account but not the identification of Samson as a judge. Judges 15:20 supports that detail.
